question.problem: A fair five-sided die with sides labeled with numbers $2,4,6,8,10$ is thrown once. If  $X$ is the outcome of the die, what is the variance of  $X?$
question.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $5$ possible outcomes ($2,4,6,8,10$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =2\cdot f(2)+4\cdot f(4)+6\cdot f(6)+8\cdot f(8)+10\cdot f(10) \\  & =2(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5})+6(\frac{1}{5})+8(\frac{1}{5})+10(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6)+{8}^{2}\cdot f(8)+{10}^{2}\cdot f(10) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{5})+16(\frac{1}{5})+36(\frac{1}{5})+64(\frac{1}{5})+100(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =44.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =44-{6}^{2} \\  & =44-36 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
